Confirmed, with one correction. The core is right and I verified it: the whole of Layer 8's specification of this target is the single bullet 'exchangeable arrays and the Aldous–Hoover representation (a substantially larger tower than the sequence theorem, with its own prerequisites)', with no statement, no hypotheses and no prerequisites, while the library has the forward direction (AldousHoover.jointArray and its exchangeability lemmas) and not the coding converse. The correction is to the clause 'The roadmap's References list no array source (Aldous 1981, Hoover 1979)'. The References section does list an array source — 'David Aldous, *Exchangeability and related topics*, École d'Été de Probabilités de Saint-Flour XIII, 1983', the standard exposition of exchangeable arrays and the Aldous–Hoover representation, and Kallenberg's *Probabilistic Symmetries and Invariance Principles*, whose Chapter 7 is the modern treatment, though it is cited there only at Chapter 1, Theorem 1.1. What is true, and is what the fix needs, is that no source is attached to the Layer 8 target and the specific papers are not listed; the Markov-exchangeability half of the clause is right, since the only Diaconis–Freedman entry is 'Finite exchangeable sequences'. The finding stands with that clause reworded.

Confirmed, and the counterexample is sound. I read both quotations in the roadmap: Layer 6 defines the family 'When `S.PosDef` and `(p : ℝ) - 1 < n`' and then says 'Define this measure to be zero when either parameter hypothesis fails', and item 4 states the congruence target for `M.rank = q` with no hypothesis beyond full row rank, justified only by 'Full row rank keeps the new scale matrix positive-definite'. At p = 2, q = 1, M = (1 0), S = 1 and n = 1/2 the source fails its own hypothesis, since 1 < 1/2 is false, so it is the zero measure and its pushforward is zero; the target is one-dimensional, where 0 < 1/2 holds and M S Mᵀ = (1) is positive definite, so it is a probability measure. Zero is not a probability measure, so the identity is false as stated, and the repair is the two hypotheses the finding names. One remark on grading, which I leave to the maintainer: section 17 reserves low for presentation, and this is a statement that is false as written, so medium would be defensible; against that, nothing is built on it yet — there is no nonsingularWishart declaration at f790474 — and the repair is to add hypotheses the author plainly intended. Confirmed. The absences check out at the pin: 'Bartlett', 'nonsingularWishart' and 'inverseWishart' return no hits in the pinned index, while every input the finding offers is present — map_cholesky_symmetricLebesgue, integral_id_inverseGammaMeasure, integrable_id_inverseGammaMeasure_iff and chiSquaredMeasure_eq_gammaMeasure. I also checked the route it proposes and it is correct: with a = (n − p + 1)/2 and r = 1/2 the inverse-gamma mean r/(a − 1) is 1/(n − p − 1), and integrability holds exactly when 1 < a, that is n > p + 1 — the mean and the threshold item 6 asks for. So the gap is real and the fix names a route that closes it.
